theory.overview: Number theory and mathematical algorithms are fundamental to cryptography, hashing, and optimization problems. Key concepts include: Sieve of Eratosthenes for prime generation, Modular Arithmetic for large number operations, GCD/LCM using Euclidean algorithm, Fast Exponentiation (binary exponentiation), and Euler's Totient function. These power RSA encryption, hash functions, and competitive programming solutions.

keyConcepts.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
keyConcepts.description: Find all primes up to n in O(n log log n). Mark multiples of each prime starting from 2. Efficient prime generation.

keyConcepts.name: Euclidean Algorithm
keyConcepts.description: Compute GCD using gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b). O(log min(a,b)). Extended version finds modular inverse.

keyConcepts.name: Modular Arithmetic
keyConcepts.description: (a + b) % mod, (a * b) % mod. Essential for large numbers. Fermat's Little Theorem: a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p) for prime p.

keyConcepts.name: Fast Exponentiation
keyConcepts.description: Compute a^b in O(log b) using binary representation of exponent. Critical for modular exponentiation in RSA.

algorithmSteps.description: Sieve: Initialize array 2..30 as potentially prime
Start with p=2. Mark all multiples as not prime.
Next unmarked is 3 (prime). Mark its multiples.
